# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+# Leaderboard submission runbook (gh-1681)
+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to
+"a submittable terminal-bench leaderboard job". Community submissions are
+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window
+reopens (2.1 today; 3.0/4.0 later), the run produced by following this
+page must already satisfy the submission rules.
+
+Sources: `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` + `core/hub.py` of the pinned dataset
+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor
+0.23.0 (`harbor upload` packager, `harbor/models/trajectories` ATIF
+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.
+
+## What the leaderboard reads
+
+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+
+- `lb filter` takes **hub job links** — a run only exists for the
+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,
+  gated on the `HARBOR_API_KEY` repo secret).
+- Leaderboard CI **re-derives every trial from the `source_jobs`** — a
+  rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable. Trials must come from ONE
+  run of the workflow.
+- The static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a hub
+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.
+- An LLM `/judge` audit runs on all successful trials (reward-hacking
+  check) — the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is the
+  mitigation; trajectories must be real, not padded.
+
+## The dispatch (submission mode)
+
+1. **Smoke first** (unchanged rule): `tasks=<family smoke>`,
+   `attempts=1`, verify the ATIF gate reports `N/N trials carry an ATIF
+   trajectory` and the uploaded smoke job shows `trajectory.json` per
+   trial on the hub. This is the AC2 verification: a 1-task smoke run
+   proves a rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory reaches the hub.
+2. **Full run**: dispatch with `submission: true` and:
+   - **no `tasks` filter** — full task coverage is required (the setup
+     preflight fails otherwise);
+   - `attempts >= 5` — at least 5 trials per task;
+   - **no `agent-timeout`** — `timeout_multiplier` must stay 1.0 (no
+     agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides);
+   - a **pinned dataset**: the full `org/name@ref` id (the preflight
+     rejects a bare name). The 2.x hub packages only carry `@latest`;
+     when it is mutable like that, record the resolved content hash
+     printed in each shard's `harbor datasets download` log into the
+     submission metadata so the submission pins what actually ran.
+
+The preflight runs in the setup job — a rule violation costs one setup
+minute, never shard-hours of un-submittable results.
+
+## Quota-window runner policy
+
+**Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded.** A
+submission job must contain **zero infra-errored trials** — never burn
+trials into a dead provider window:
+
+- Provider quota windows (e.g. the Kimi coding plan's 5-hour windows)
+  are handled **runner-side**: the runner waits between trials (the
+  workflow's progress-watch kill + `n-concurrent: 1` keep every trial
+  inside a live window); no trial is started into a dead window.
+- This supersedes the closed #1674 **in the bench context**: fail-fast
+  stays the default for local runs; the leaderboard-configured runner
+  parks between trials instead of burning attempts.
+- If a shard still ends with errored trials (exception classes in the
+  summary's erored-trials breakdown), the run is not submittable —
+  rerun the shard matrix fresh rather than stitching.
+
+## Verifying readiness after the run
+
+1. The job summary shows the **ATIF trajectories** block per shard
+   (`N/N trials carry an ATIF trajectory`); with `submission: true` any
+   miss fails the shard before upload.
+2. Each shard's **Upload to Harbor Hub** step logs the uploaded job;
+   open the hub job and confirm the trials are **publicly readable** and
+   each carries a `trajectory.json`.
+3. `result.json` metadata carries `atif_trajectory: present|missing`
+   (folded by the adapter) so the ledger can be audited without the hub.
+
+## Submitting (when a window reopens)
+
+Per the dataset repo's `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`:
+
+1. `lb filter` — submit the hub job links from the run (one submission
+   per agent + agent version + model + reasoning effort; the workflow's
+   run label and `fa --version` identify the pair).
+2. `lb metadata` — attach the run metadata (dataset id + resolved
+   content hash for `@latest` families, model, agent version, date).
+3. `lb open-prs` — open the submission PRs.
+4. The `/judge` reward-hacking audit runs on all successful trials
+   automatically.
+
+## Failure modes and what to do
+
+| Symptom | Meaning | Action |
+|---|---|---|
+| Preflight ATIF step warns `X/Y` in a normal run | a trial finished without a trajectory | check the shard log for the `[fa_agent] warning: ATIF trajectory export` line; rerun the shard |
+| Submission-mode shard fails at the ATIF gate | un-submittable job caught before upload | fix, rerun the shard fresh (no stitching) |
+| Setup preflight rejects the dispatch | a submission rule violated (coverage, attempts, timeout override, unpinned dataset) | re-dispatch with the rule satisfied |
+| Hub upload step skipped | `HARBOR_API_KEY` secret absent | owner provisions the secret; artifacts still carry results |

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# Leaderboard submission runbook (gh-1681)
+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to
+"a submittable terminal-bench leaderboard job". Community submissions are
+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window
+reopens (2.1 today; 3.0/4.0 later), the run produced by following this
+page must already satisfy the submission rules.
+
+Sources: `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` + `core/hub.py` of the pinned dataset
+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor
+0.23.0 (`harbor upload` packager, `harbor/models/trajectories` ATIF
+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.
+
+## What the leaderboard reads
+
+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+
+- `lb filter` takes **hub job links** — a run only exists for the
+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,
+  gated on the `HARBOR_API_KEY` repo secret).
+- Leaderboard CI **re-derives every trial from the `source_jobs`** — a
+  rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable. Trials must come from ONE
+  run of the workflow.
+- The static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a hub
+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.
+- An LLM `/judge` audit runs on all successful trials (reward-hacking

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# Leaderboard submission runbook (gh-1681)
+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to
+"a submittable terminal-bench leaderboard job". Community submissions are
+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window
+reopens (2.1 today; 3.0/4.0 later), the run produced by following this
+page must already satisfy the submission rules.
+
+Sources: `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` + `core/hub.py` of the pinned dataset
+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor
+0.23.0 (`harbor upload` packager, `harbor/models/trajectories` ATIF
+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.
+
+## What the leaderboard reads
+
+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+
+- `lb filter` takes **hub job links** — a run only exists for the
+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,
+  gated on the `HARBOR_API_KEY` repo secret).
+- Leaderboard CI **re-derives every trial from the `source_jobs`** — a
+  rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable. Trials must come from ONE
+  run of the workflow.
+- The static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a hub
+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.
+- An LLM `/judge` audit runs on all successful trials (reward-hacking
+  check) — the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is the
+  mitigation; trajectories must be real, n…

+    - the `submission` dispatch input exists, boolean, OFF by default
+      (AC4: no change to default bench behavior);
+    - the setup job gains a submission preflight (full coverage, >=5
+      attempts/task, no agent-timeout override, pinned dataset) gated on
+      that input;
+    - each shard gains an ATIF presence gate before the hub upload
+      (warn-only normally, hard failure in submission mode);
+    - the hub upload step itself keeps its secret-gated always-skip
+      shape.
+    """
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.text = _HARBOR_YML.read_text()
+        setup_end = cls.text.index("\n  bench:")
+        cls.setup_job = cls.text[:setup_end]
+        cls.bench_job = cls.text[setup_end:cls.text.index("\n  summary:")]
+
+    def test_submission_input_is_boolean_off_by_default(self):
+        block = self.text.split("submission:", 1)[1].split("permissions:", 1)[0]
+        self.assertIn("type: boolean", block)
+        self.assertIn("default: false", block)
+
+    def test_setup_preflight_is_submission_gated(self):
+        self.assertIn("if: inputs.submission == true", self.setup_job)
+        self.assertIn("Leaderboard submission preflight", self.setup_job)
+        # The preflight must run BEFORE the bundle build / shard split
+        # (it is part of the setup job at all) and enforce every rule.
+        for rule in (
+            "full task coverage",
+            "attempts >= 5",
+            "timeout_multiplier 1.0",
+            "org/name@ref",
+        ):
+            self.assertIn(rule, self.setup_job)
+
+    def test_atif_gate_sits_before_the_hub_upload(self):
+        self.assertIn("Preflight ATIF trajectories", self.bench_job)
+        self.assertLess(
+            self.bench_job.index("Preflight ATIF trajectories"),
+            self.bench_job.index("Upload to Harbor Hub"),
+        )
+        gate = self.bench_job.split("Preflight ATIF trajectories", 1)[1]
+        gate = gate.split("Upload to Harbor Hub", 1)[0]
+        # Warn-only normally; submission mode fails hard; the scan covers
+        # agent/trajectory.json per trial dir with a result.json.
+        self.assertIn('SUBMISSION: ${{ inputs.submission }}', gate)
+        self.assertIn("agent/trajectory.json", gate)
+        self.assertIn("exit 1", gate)
+
+    def test_hub_upload_stays_secret_gated_and_public(self):
+        upload = self.bench_job.split("Upload to Harbor Hub", 1)[1]
+        upload = upload.split("- name:", 1)[0]
+        self.assertIn("if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''", upload)
+        self.assertIn("harbor upload", upload)
+        self.assertIn("--public", upload)
+
+    def test_default_dispatch_has_no_submission_side_effects(self):
+        # AC4: without submission=true the only new behavior is the
+        # always-on warn-only ATIF scan; the preflight step must not run.
+        preflight = self.setup_job.split("Leaderboard submission preflight", 1)
+        self.assertEqual(len(preflight), 2)
+        self.assertIn("if: inputs.submission == true", preflight[1][:200])
+
+

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. # gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# Leaderboard submission runbook (gh-1681)
+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to
+"a submittable terminal-bench leaderboard job". Community submissions are
+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window
+reopens (2.1 today; 3.0/4.0 later), the run produced by following this
+page must already satisfy the submission rules.
+
+Sources: `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` + `core/hub.py` of the pinned dataset
+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor
+0.23.0 (`harbor upload` packager, `harbor/models/trajectories` ATIF
+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.
+
+## What the leaderboard reads
+
+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+
+- `lb filter` takes **hub job links** — a run only exists for the
+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,
+  gated on the `HARBOR_API_KEY` repo secret).
+- Leaderboard CI **re-derives every trial from the `source_jobs`** — a
+  rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable. Trials must come from ONE
+  run of the workflow.
+- The static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a hub
+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.
+- An LLM `/judge` audit runs on all successful trials (reward-hacking
+  check) — the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is the
+  mitigation; trajectories must be real, n…

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+

# gh-1681: [GOAL] Leaderboard submission readiness: Harbor hub upload + ATIF trajectories + quota-safe runner policy

## Description

### Goal

Make bench-harbor runs **leaderboard-submittable** to terminal-bench (2.1 today, 3.0/4.0 when community submissions reopen — currently all closed: "only submissions run by the maintainers"). Two gaps block submission readiness today:

### Gap 1 — Harbor Hub upload (`harbor run --upload`)

The leaderboard pipeline (`leaderboard/SUBMIT.md`, harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1) reads everything from the Harbor hub: `lb filter` takes hub job links, CI re-derives every trial from hub, `/judge` audits hub trajectories. Our `bench-harbor.yml` only uploads GitHub Actions artifacts — trials never reach the hub.

- Add a hub-upload leg to the bench workflow (hub auth via a repo secret, upload after each shard or at aggregate; `--upload` at run time or post-hoc upload both allowed by their docs).
- Trials must be **publicly readable** on hub.harborframework.com.

### Gap 2 — ATIF trajectory readiness

Static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a Hub `trajectory_path` (ATIF format) — "agents that only upload custom logs fail here". Our fa adapter writes fa JSONL sessions; we must verify that harbor itself converts/stores an ATIF trajectory for installed agents, or add an ATIF export path (`lib/src/trajectory/` already has whole-snapshot exporters — the natural home).

### Submission rules that shape the run (encode as a preflight checklist in the workflow/docs)

- Exact pinned dataset (`DATASET@DATASET_REF` from their `core/hub.py`), `timeout_multiplier` 1.0, no agent/verifier timeout overrides, no resource overrides — CI rejects otherwise.
- Full task coverage, ≥5 trials/task. **Errored trials count as reward 0 and are NOT excluded** — a submission job must contain zero infra-errored trials. Practical consequence: provider quota windows (Kimi 5-hour limit) must be handled by RUNNER-side waiting between trials (no trial is started into a dead window), never by burning trials — a rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable because CI re-derives all trials from `source_jobs`. (Supersedes the closed #1674 in the bench context specifically: fail-fast stays for local runs, but the leaderboard-configured runner parks between trials.)
- One submission per (agent, agent version, model, reasoning effort); metadata via `lb metadata`; PR flow via `lb open-prs`; LLM `/judge` reward-hacking audit on all successful trials (the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is our friend here).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `bench-harbor.yml` gains a hub-upload path (secret-gated; off by default until hub credentials exist).
2. A rewarded trial's ATIF trajectory is present on the hub after upload (verified on a 1-task smoke run).
3. `docs/` gains a "leaderboard submission runbook": dataset pin check, quota-window runner policy, lb CLI steps.
4. No change to default bench behavior (artifact flow stays as-is when hub upload is off).

### References

- harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` (submission rules, lb CLI, /judge pipeline).
- Community submissions closed at the time of writing for 2.1 and 4.0 — this card is readiness, not an immediate submission.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# Leaderboard submission runbook (gh-1681)
+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to
+"a submittable terminal-bench leaderboard job". Community submissions are
+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window
+reopens (2.1 today; 3.0/4.0 later), the run produced by following this
+page must already satisfy the submission rules.
+
+Sources: `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` + `core/hub.py` of the pinned dataset
+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor
+0.23.0 (`harbor upload` packager, `harbor/models/trajectories` ATIF
+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.
+
+## What the leaderboard reads
+
+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+
+- `lb filter` takes **hub job links** — a run only exists for the
+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,
+  gated on the `HARBOR_API_KEY` repo secret).
+- Leaderboard CI **re-derives every trial from the `source_jobs`** — a
+  rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable. Trials must come from ONE
+  run of the workflow.
+- The static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a hub
+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.
+- An LLM `/judge` audit runs on all successful trials (reward-hacking
+  check) — the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is the
+  mitigation; trajectories must be real, n…

+@unittest.skipUnless(

+class SubmissionPreflightWiringTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """gh-1681: leaderboard submission readiness wiring.
+
+    - the `submission` dispatch input exists, boolean, OFF by default
+      (AC4: no change to default bench behavior);
+    - the setup job gains a submission preflight (full coverage, >=5
+      attempts/task, no agent-timeout override, pinned dataset) gated on
+      that input;
+    - each shard gains an ATIF presence gate before the hub upload
+      (warn-only normally, hard failure in submission mode);
+    - the hub upload step itself keeps its secret-gated always-skip
+      shape.
+    """
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.text = _HARBOR_YML.read_text()
+        setup_end = cls.text.index("\n  bench:")

+        cls.bench_job = cls.text[setup_end:cls.text.index("\n  summary:")]
+

+        self.assertIn("if: inputs.submission == true", self.setup_job)
+        self.assertIn("Leaderboard submission preflight", self.setup_job)
+        # The preflight must run BEFORE the bundle build / shard split
+        # (it is part of the setup job at all) and enforce every rule.

+            "full task coverage",
+            "attempts >= 5",
+            "timeout_multiplier 1.0",
+            "org/name@ref",
+        ):
+            self.assertIn(rule, self.setup_job)
+
+    def test_atif_gate_sits_before_the_hub_upload(self):
+        self.assertIn("Preflight ATIF trajectories", self.bench_job)
+        self.assertLess(
+            self.bench_job.index("Preflight ATIF trajectories"),
+            self.bench_job.index("Upload to Harbor Hub"),
