# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Conventions noted. The barrel export policy says GROUPED APPEND-ONLY exports with sorted-by-path within a group. The diff added `export 'src/trajectory/atif_export.dart';` after `search_index.dart` — within the trajectory group; `atif_export.dart` alphabetically sorts before `search_index.dart`... but the policy says "exports sorted by path within a group, new exports appended to their subsystem group". Let me check the group context in the barrel to see if placement violates sort order.
{"command":"cd /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness && sed -n '228,245p' lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart"}

The trajectory group is not strictly sorted anyway (timeline_projection, trajectory_record, event_projection...), and the policy is append-only — the new export was appended to the end of the trajectory group. Fine.

Now let me check the integration test result, and look at the truncated portion of the diff I haven't reviewed — mostly test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart (already seen the tail). Also pr_discussions_raw.json — quick check. Then assess workflow security/CI safety:

Workflow checks:
- New `submission` input: boolean, default false. OK.
- Preflight step: gated `if: inputs.submission == true`. Uses `env:` for inputs — good (no script injection; inputs are expressions in env). DATASET/TASKS/ATTEMPTS/AGENT_TIMEOUT all via env. Good.
- ATIF gate: `if: always()` — env from matrix values via expressions. Shell script uses nullglob, quotes variables. Good.
- No new secrets, no permissions changes. `--public` upload remains. Ticket AC1 wants public trials — consistent.
- The upload step iterates `fa-${FAMILY}-*` — with ATIF gate before it failing the job in submission mode... but upload step is `if: always()` so it still runs after gate failure! Wait: if the ATIF gate exits 1, the job is marked failed, but subsequent `if: always()` steps still run — including "Upload to Harbor Hub". The gate's stated purpose: "hard failure in submission mode (an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either)". But since the upload step is `if: always()`, a failed ATIF gate does NOT prevent the upload from happening! The job will fail overall, but the upload still burns hub quota — contradicting the comment's claim. Let me check the order and whether upload is `if: always()`.

From the diff earlier: `- name: Upload to Harbor Hub / if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. And the ATIF gate runs BEFORE it (test asserted ordering). But `if: always()` on the upload means it runs even when the ATIF gate failed. So in submission mode with missing trajectories: gate fails the job → but upload proceeds anyway. The gate "fails hard" the shard, but does not gate the upload. That's a real inconsistency with the design intent stated in the step comment ("an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either"). 

Hmm wait — but failing the shard means the trial results aren't submittable anyway; uploading a failed job is wasted hub quota. The comment explicitly claims the hard failure prevents burning quota, which is wrong. Is this BLOCKING? It doesn't break default behavior; it's a submission-mode wart. The failure is still surfaced and the shard marked failed. I'd classify IMPORTANT: either make the upload condition `success() ||` skip when the gate failed in submission mode (e.g. `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != '' && !(inputs.submission && failed gate)`), or fix the comment. Given submission mode is new and off by default, this is a correctness gap in the new feature's stated guarantee → IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING for the feature's stated contract, but nothing silently wrong; the shard still fails). I'll mark IMPORTANT.

Also check: the workflow test `test_atif_gate_sits_before_the_hub_upload` only asserts ordering, not the `if:` interplay — hence the gap went untested.

Another point: the ATIF gate summary says "X/Y trials carry an ATIF trajectory" — when JOB dir doesn't exist at all (zero-trial total failure), the glob is null, total=0 → "0/0" and in submission mode `missing=0` → no failure from this step. But the harbor run step already failed → job failed. OK.

Now also check the "warning" message in normal mode references the leaderboard — fine.

Python: `_export_atif_trajectory` catches `Exception` — but not `BaseException`; CanceledError propagates. During external cancel, finally runs the export; the test asserts it completes. Fine.

One more: the export exec's command: `fa --session-root /logs/agent/fah-sessions trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json`. The export resolves "most recent session" when no sessionId given. If the session root contains multiple sessions (unlikely in bench), it picks the most recent — reasonable.

But wait — an important one: **does the in-container fa write the session JSONL under a cwd-encoded subdir of the session root?** `_runTrajectoryCommand` computes `sessionRoot = args.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()` and JsonlSessionRepo(sessionsRoot: sessionRoot). resolveTrajectorySession presumably scans subdirs. Fine.

**Another potential issue**: gh-1589 headless sealing — "no session-JSONL writes land after the run's agent phase ends". The export only reads. OK.

**Timeout**: `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SEC + 15)` around `exec_as_agent(timeout_sec=180)`. exec_as_agent's timeout_sec presumably kills in-container process. Fine.

Now — ci_failures.md is absent from input. The discussions mention an earlier red that was fixed by rework (bench script test updated). Current head 1e6bef4 is a merge of main. I can't verify current CI status locally; I'll note the earlier red was addressed and that there's no ci_failures input.

Let me check the integration test job result, and read pr_discussions_raw.json quickly.

content.text:
# per trial — the leaderboard static analysis requires one on every
# rewarded trial — and the `submission` input turns the submission rules
# (leaderboard/SUBMIT.md of the pinned terminal-bench dataset repo) into
# hard preflight gates. See docs/leaderboard-submission.md.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe; the kimi coding plan tolerates more — owner picks at dispatch)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      submission:
        description: 'gh-1681: leaderboard submission mode — the setup preflight enforces the submission rules (full task coverage, >=5 attempts/task, no agent-timeout override, pinned dataset) and the per-shard ATIF gate fails hard when a trial lacks agent/trajectory.json. See docs/leaderboard-submission.md'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched

@@ -0,0 +1,92 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):

+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to

+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window

+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor

+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.

+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+

+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,

+  run of the workflow.

+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.

+  check) — the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is the
+  mitigation; trajectories must be real, n…

if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          # gh-1600: iterate the out-of-workspace output dir (see the harbor
          # run step).
          for job_dir in "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

      # gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Conventions noted. The barrel export policy says GROUPED APPEND-ONLY exports with sorted-by-path within a group. The diff added `export 'src/trajectory/atif_export.dart';` after `search_index.dart` — within the trajectory group; `atif_export.dart` alphabetically sorts before `search_index.dart`... but the policy says "exports sorted by path within a group, new exports appended to their subsystem group". Let me check the group context in the barrel to see if placement violates sort order.
{"command":"cd /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness && sed -n '228,245p' lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart"}

The trajectory group is not strictly sorted anyway (timeline_projection, trajectory_record, event_projection...), and the policy is append-only — the new export was appended to the end of the trajectory group. Fine.

Now let me check the integration test result, and look at the truncated portion of the diff I haven't reviewed — mostly test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart (already seen the tail). Also pr_discussions_raw.json — quick check. Then assess workflow security/CI safety:

Workflow checks:
- New `submission` input: boolean, default false. OK.
- Preflight step: gated `if: inputs.submission == true`. Uses `env:` for inputs — good (no script injection; inputs are expressions in env). DATASET/TASKS/ATTEMPTS/AGENT_TIMEOUT all via env. Good.
- ATIF gate: `if: always()` — env from matrix values via expressions. Shell script uses nullglob, quotes variables. Good.
- No new secrets, no permissions changes. `--public` upload remains. Ticket AC1 wants public trials — consistent.
- The upload step iterates `fa-${FAMILY}-*` — with ATIF gate before it failing the job in submission mode... but upload step is `if: always()` so it still runs after gate failure! Wait: if the ATIF gate exits 1, the job is marked failed, but subsequent `if: always()` steps still run — including "Upload to Harbor Hub". The gate's stated purpose: "hard failure in submission mode (an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either)". But since the upload step is `if: always()`, a failed ATIF gate does NOT prevent the upload from happening! The job will fail overall, but the upload still burns hub quota — contradicting the comment's claim. Let me check the order and whether upload is `if: always()`.

From the diff earlier: `- name: Upload to Harbor Hub / if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. And the ATIF gate runs BEFORE it (test asserted ordering). But `if: always()` on the upload means it runs even when the ATIF gate failed. So in submission mode with missing trajectories: gate fails the job → but upload proceeds anyway. The gate "fails hard" the shard, but does not gate the upload. That's a real inconsistency with the design intent stated in the step comment ("an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either"). 

Hmm wait — but failing the shard means the trial results aren't submittable anyway; uploading a failed job is wasted hub quota. The comment explicitly claims the hard failure prevents burning quota, which is wrong. Is this BLOCKING? It doesn't break default behavior; it's a submission-mode wart. The failure is still surfaced and the shard marked failed. I'd classify IMPORTANT: either make the upload condition `success() ||` skip when the gate failed in submission mode (e.g. `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != '' && !(inputs.submission && failed gate)`), or fix the comment. Given submission mode is new and off by default, this is a correctness gap in the new feature's stated guarantee → IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING for the feature's stated contract, but nothing silently wrong; the shard still fails). I'll mark IMPORTANT.

Also check: the workflow test `test_atif_gate_sits_before_the_hub_upload` only asserts ordering, not the `if:` interplay — hence the gap went untested.

Another point: the ATIF gate summary says "X/Y trials carry an ATIF trajectory" — when JOB dir doesn't exist at all (zero-trial total failure), the glob is null, total=0 → "0/0" and in submission mode `missing=0` → no failure from this step. But the harbor run step already failed → job failed. OK.

Now also check the "warning" message in normal mode references the leaderboard — fine.

Python: `_export_atif_trajectory` catches `Exception` — but not `BaseException`; CanceledError propagates. During external cancel, finally runs the export; the test asserts it completes. Fine.

One more: the export exec's command: `fa --session-root /logs/agent/fah-sessions trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json`. The export resolves "most recent session" when no sessionId given. If the session root contains multiple sessions (unlikely in bench), it picks the most recent — reasonable.

But wait — an important one: **does the in-container fa write the session JSONL under a cwd-encoded subdir of the session root?** `_runTrajectoryCommand` computes `sessionRoot = args.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()` and JsonlSessionRepo(sessionsRoot: sessionRoot). resolveTrajectorySession presumably scans subdirs. Fine.

**Another potential issue**: gh-1589 headless sealing — "no session-JSONL writes land after the run's agent phase ends". The export only reads. OK.

**Timeout**: `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SEC + 15)` around `exec_as_agent(timeout_sec=180)`. exec_as_agent's timeout_sec presumably kills in-container process. Fine.

Now — ci_failures.md is absent from input. The discussions mention an earlier red that was fixed by rework (bench script test updated). Current head 1e6bef4 is a merge of main. I can't verify current CI status locally; I'll note the earlier red was addressed and that there's no ci_failures input.

Let me check the integration test job result, and read pr_discussions_raw.json quickly.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""gh-1681 Gap 2 — the ATIF fixture contract, validated from the harbor side.
+
+`bench/harbor_fa/fixtures/atif_sample.json` is the GOLDEN output of the
+Dart exporter (`lib/src/trajectory/atif_export.dart`, pinned by
+test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart). This test loads the same bytes and
+validates them against the REAL harbor 0.23.0 trajectory stack — the
+pydantic `Trajectory` model and the static-analysis
+`validate_trajectory` gate — so a schema drift on either side fails the
+bench-script gate the workflows run (bench-tests.yml installs the pinned
+harbor; the test skips when harbor is not importable, e.g. a bare dev
+box).
+
+Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa
+"""
+import json
+import shutil
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+_FIXTURE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "fixtures" / "atif_sample.json"
+
+try:
+    from harbor.models.trajectories.trajectory import Trajectory
+    from harbor.utils.trajectory_validator import validate_trajectory
+
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - exercised on bare dev boxes
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE = False
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _HARBOR_AVAILABLE,
+    "harbor not importable (install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0' as the "
+    "bench workflows do)",
+)
+class AtifFixtureContractTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Dart exporter's golden output must satisfy harbor's model and
+    the leaderboard-style static validator."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.data = json.loads(_FIXTURE.read_text())
+
+    def test_fixture_parses_as_atif_trajectory(self):
+        trajectory = Trajectory(**self.data)
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.schema_version, "ATIF-v1.7")
+        self.assertEqual(trajectory.agent.name, "fa")
+        self.assertEqual(len(trajectory.steps), 7)
+        # Step ids are sequential from 1 (the model enforces it too).
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [s.step_id for s in trajectory.steps], list(range(1, 8))
+        )
+
+    def test_fixture_passes_the_static_analysis_validator(self):
+        self.assertTrue(validate_trajectory(self.data))
+
+    def test_tool_steps_are_deterministic_dispatches(self):
+        tool_steps = [
+            s for s in self.data["steps"] if "tool_calls" in s
+        ]
+        self.assertTrue(tool_steps)
+        for step in tool_steps:
+            self.assertEqual(step["llm_call_count"], 0)
+            self.assertNotIn("metrics", step)
+            self.assertNotIn("reasoning_content", step)
+            self.assertIn("message", step)  # required on every step
+
+    def test_non_agent_steps_carry_no_agent_only_fields(self):
+        for step in self.data["steps"]:
+            if step["source"] == "agent":
+                continue
+            for key in (
+                "model_name",
+                "metrics",
+                "tool_calls",
+                "reasoning_content",
+                "llm_call_count",
+            ):
+                self.assertNotIn(key, step, f"{key} on {step['source']} step")
+
+    def test_final_metrics_totals_match_the_steps(self):
+        metrics = self.data["final_metrics"]
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_steps"], len(self.data["steps"]))
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_prompt_tokens"], 100)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_completion_tokens"], 20)
+        self.assertEqual(metrics["total_cached_tokens"], 30)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# Leaderboard submission runbook (gh-1681)
+
+How to take a `bench-harbor.yml` run from "results on the Harbor Hub" to
+"a submittable terminal-bench leaderboard job". Community submissions are
+currently closed for every terminal-bench version ("only submissions run
+by the maintainers") — this is **readiness**: when a submission window
+reopens (2.1 today; 3.0/4.0 later), the run produced by following this
+page must already satisfy the submission rules.
+
+Sources: `leaderboard/SUBMIT.md` + `core/hub.py` of the pinned dataset
+repo (harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1 for the 2.1 family), harbor
+0.23.0 (`harbor upload` packager, `harbor/models/trajectories` ATIF
+schema), and the `submission: true` preflight in
+`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`.
+
+## What the leaderboard reads
+
+Everything comes from the Harbor Hub (`hub.harborframework.com`):
+
+- `lb filter` takes **hub job links** — a run only exists for the
+  leaderboard if every shard was uploaded (`harbor upload --public`,
+  gated on the `HARBOR_API_KEY` repo secret).
+- Leaderboard CI **re-derives every trial from the `source_jobs`** — a
+  rerun-stitched matrix is not submittable. Trials must come from ONE
+  run of the workflow.
+- The static analysis requires every rewarded trial to have a hub
+  `trajectory_path` in **ATIF format** — "agents that only upload custom
+  logs fail here". The fa adapter exports
+  `<trial>/agent/trajectory.json` per trial (`fa trajectory export
+  --format atif`, gh-1681 Gap 2) and the per-shard **Preflight ATIF
+  trajectories** step verifies presence before upload.
+- An LLM `/judge` audit runs on all successful trials (reward-hacking
+  check) — the finalize gate's verify-before-claim discipline is the
+  mitigation; trajectories must be real, n…

if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          # gh-1600: iterate the out-of-workspace output dir (see the harbor
          # run step).
          for job_dir in "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

      # gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to ${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Conventions noted. The barrel export policy says GROUPED APPEND-ONLY exports with sorted-by-path within a group. The diff added `export 'src/trajectory/atif_export.dart';` after `search_index.dart` — within the trajectory group; `atif_export.dart` alphabetically sorts before `search_index.dart`... but the policy says "exports sorted by path within a group, new exports appended to their subsystem group". Let me check the group context in the barrel to see if placement violates sort order.
{"command":"cd /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness && sed -n '228,245p' lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart"}

The trajectory group is not strictly sorted anyway (timeline_projection, trajectory_record, event_projection...), and the policy is append-only — the new export was appended to the end of the trajectory group. Fine.

Now let me check the integration test result, and look at the truncated portion of the diff I haven't reviewed — mostly test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart (already seen the tail). Also pr_discussions_raw.json — quick check. Then assess workflow security/CI safety:

Workflow checks:
- New `submission` input: boolean, default false. OK.
- Preflight step: gated `if: inputs.submission == true`. Uses `env:` for inputs — good (no script injection; inputs are expressions in env). DATASET/TASKS/ATTEMPTS/AGENT_TIMEOUT all via env. Good.
- ATIF gate: `if: always()` — env from matrix values via expressions. Shell script uses nullglob, quotes variables. Good.
- No new secrets, no permissions changes. `--public` upload remains. Ticket AC1 wants public trials — consistent.
- The upload step iterates `fa-${FAMILY}-*` — with ATIF gate before it failing the job in submission mode... but upload step is `if: always()` so it still runs after gate failure! Wait: if the ATIF gate exits 1, the job is marked failed, but subsequent `if: always()` steps still run — including "Upload to Harbor Hub". The gate's stated purpose: "hard failure in submission mode (an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either)". But since the upload step is `if: always()`, a failed ATIF gate does NOT prevent the upload from happening! The job will fail overall, but the upload still burns hub quota — contradicting the comment's claim. Let me check the order and whether upload is `if: always()`.

From the diff earlier: `- name: Upload to Harbor Hub / if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. And the ATIF gate runs BEFORE it (test asserted ordering). But `if: always()` on the upload means it runs even when the ATIF gate failed. So in submission mode with missing trajectories: gate fails the job → but upload proceeds anyway. The gate "fails hard" the shard, but does not gate the upload. That's a real inconsistency with the design intent stated in the step comment ("an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either"). 

Hmm wait — but failing the shard means the trial results aren't submittable anyway; uploading a failed job is wasted hub quota. The comment explicitly claims the hard failure prevents burning quota, which is wrong. Is this BLOCKING? It doesn't break default behavior; it's a submission-mode wart. The failure is still surfaced and the shard marked failed. I'd classify IMPORTANT: either make the upload condition `success() ||` skip when the gate failed in submission mode (e.g. `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != '' && !(inputs.submission && failed gate)`), or fix the comment. Given submission mode is new and off by default, this is a correctness gap in the new feature's stated guarantee → IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING for the feature's stated contract, but nothing silently wrong; the shard still fails). I'll mark IMPORTANT.

Also check: the workflow test `test_atif_gate_sits_before_the_hub_upload` only asserts ordering, not the `if:` interplay — hence the gap went untested.

Another point: the ATIF gate summary says "X/Y trials carry an ATIF trajectory" — when JOB dir doesn't exist at all (zero-trial total failure), the glob is null, total=0 → "0/0" and in submission mode `missing=0` → no failure from this step. But the harbor run step already failed → job failed. OK.

Now also check the "warning" message in normal mode references the leaderboard — fine.

Python: `_export_atif_trajectory` catches `Exception` — but not `BaseException`; CanceledError propagates. During external cancel, finally runs the export; the test asserts it completes. Fine.

One more: the export exec's command: `fa --session-root /logs/agent/fah-sessions trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json`. The export resolves "most recent session" when no sessionId given. If the session root contains multiple sessions (unlikely in bench), it picks the most recent — reasonable.

But wait — an important one: **does the in-container fa write the session JSONL under a cwd-encoded subdir of the session root?** `_runTrajectoryCommand` computes `sessionRoot = args.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()` and JsonlSessionRepo(sessionsRoot: sessionRoot). resolveTrajectorySession presumably scans subdirs. Fine.

**Another potential issue**: gh-1589 headless sealing — "no session-JSONL writes land after the run's agent phase ends". The export only reads. OK.

**Timeout**: `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SEC + 15)` around `exec_as_agent(timeout_sec=180)`. exec_as_agent's timeout_sec presumably kills in-container process. Fine.

Now — ci_failures.md is absent from input. The discussions mention an earlier red that was fixed by rework (bench script test updated). Current head 1e6bef4 is a merge of main. I can't verify current CI status locally; I'll note the earlier red was addressed and that there's no ci_failures input.

Let me check the integration test job result, and read pr_discussions_raw.json quickly.

if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          # gh-1600: iterate the out-of-workspace output dir (see the harbor
          # run step).
          for job_dir in "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

      # gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to ${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Conventions noted. The barrel export policy says GROUPED APPEND-ONLY exports with sorted-by-path within a group. The diff added `export 'src/trajectory/atif_export.dart';` after `search_index.dart` — within the trajectory group; `atif_export.dart` alphabetically sorts before `search_index.dart`... but the policy says "exports sorted by path within a group, new exports appended to their subsystem group". Let me check the group context in the barrel to see if placement violates sort order.
{"command":"cd /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness && sed -n '228,245p' lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart"}

The trajectory group is not strictly sorted anyway (timeline_projection, trajectory_record, event_projection...), and the policy is append-only — the new export was appended to the end of the trajectory group. Fine.

Now let me check the integration test result, and look at the truncated portion of the diff I haven't reviewed — mostly test/trajectory/atif_export_test.dart (already seen the tail). Also pr_discussions_raw.json — quick check. Then assess workflow security/CI safety:

Workflow checks:
- New `submission` input: boolean, default false. OK.
- Preflight step: gated `if: inputs.submission == true`. Uses `env:` for inputs — good (no script injection; inputs are expressions in env). DATASET/TASKS/ATTEMPTS/AGENT_TIMEOUT all via env. Good.
- ATIF gate: `if: always()` — env from matrix values via expressions. Shell script uses nullglob, quotes variables. Good.
- No new secrets, no permissions changes. `--public` upload remains. Ticket AC1 wants public trials — consistent.
- The upload step iterates `fa-${FAMILY}-*` — with ATIF gate before it failing the job in submission mode... but upload step is `if: always()` so it still runs after gate failure! Wait: if the ATIF gate exits 1, the job is marked failed, but subsequent `if: always()` steps still run — including "Upload to Harbor Hub". The gate's stated purpose: "hard failure in submission mode (an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either)". But since the upload step is `if: always()`, a failed ATIF gate does NOT prevent the upload from happening! The job will fail overall, but the upload still burns hub quota — contradicting the comment's claim. Let me check the order and whether upload is `if: always()`.

From the diff earlier: `- name: Upload to Harbor Hub / if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''`. And the ATIF gate runs BEFORE it (test asserted ordering). But `if: always()` on the upload means it runs even when the ATIF gate failed. So in submission mode with missing trajectories: gate fails the job → but upload proceeds anyway. The gate "fails hard" the shard, but does not gate the upload. That's a real inconsistency with the design intent stated in the step comment ("an un-submittable job must not burn hub quota either"). 

Hmm wait — but failing the shard means the trial results aren't submittable anyway; uploading a failed job is wasted hub quota. The comment explicitly claims the hard failure prevents burning quota, which is wrong. Is this BLOCKING? It doesn't break default behavior; it's a submission-mode wart. The failure is still surfaced and the shard marked failed. I'd classify IMPORTANT: either make the upload condition `success() ||` skip when the gate failed in submission mode (e.g. `if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != '' && !(inputs.submission && failed gate)`), or fix the comment. Given submission mode is new and off by default, this is a correctness gap in the new feature's stated guarantee → IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING for the feature's stated contract, but nothing silently wrong; the shard still fails). I'll mark IMPORTANT.

Also check: the workflow test `test_atif_gate_sits_before_the_hub_upload` only asserts ordering, not the `if:` interplay — hence the gap went untested.

Another point: the ATIF gate summary says "X/Y trials carry an ATIF trajectory" — when JOB dir doesn't exist at all (zero-trial total failure), the glob is null, total=0 → "0/0" and in submission mode `missing=0` → no failure from this step. But the harbor run step already failed → job failed. OK.

Now also check the "warning" message in normal mode references the leaderboard — fine.

Python: `_export_atif_trajectory` catches `Exception` — but not `BaseException`; CanceledError propagates. During external cancel, finally runs the export; the test asserts it completes. Fine.

One more: the export exec's command: `fa --session-root /logs/agent/fah-sessions trajectory export --format atif --output /logs/agent/trajectory.json`. The export resolves "most recent session" when no sessionId given. If the session root contains multiple sessions (unlikely in bench), it picks the most recent — reasonable.

But wait — an important one: **does the in-container fa write the session JSONL under a cwd-encoded subdir of the session root?** `_runTrajectoryCommand` computes `sessionRoot = args.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()` and JsonlSessionRepo(sessionsRoot: sessionRoot). resolveTrajectorySession presumably scans subdirs. Fine.

**Another potential issue**: gh-1589 headless sealing — "no session-JSONL writes land after the run's agent phase ends". The export only reads. OK.

**Timeout**: `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SEC + 15)` around `exec_as_agent(timeout_sec=180)`. exec_as_agent's timeout_sec presumably kills in-container process. Fine.

Now — ci_failures.md is absent from input. The discussions mention an earlier red that was fixed by rework (bench script test updated). Current head 1e6bef4 is a merge of main. I can't verify current CI status locally; I'll note the earlier red was addressed and that there's no ci_failures input.

Let me check the integration test job result, and read pr_discussions_raw.json quickly.

        required: false

blocks.text:
if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          # gh-1600: iterate the out-of-workspace output dir (see the harbor
          # run step).
          for job_dir in "$RUNNER_TEMP/bench/jobs"/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

      # gh-1600 AC2: a cancelled/interrupted shard can leave the trial
      # containers (and their bind mounts over the output dir) alive on the
      # persistent self-hosted box — those holds made the NEXT workflow's
      # workspace clean fail. Tear the shard's containers down BEFORE
      # removing the output dir; both are best-effort (the uploads above
      # already ran) so cleanup can never mask the shard's verdict.
      - name: Tear down bench containers + output dir (gh-1600)
        if: always()
        env:
          # ENV_TYPE is scoped to the harbor-run step above — the cleanup
          # needs its own copy or `set -u` kills it ("ENV_TYPE: unbound
          # variable") and the always() step fails the job.
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # gh-1600 rework round 2 (BLOCKING review thread, re-opened):
            # harbor 0.23.0 never puts the job name in container names
            # (compose project = `{task}__{ShortUUID(7)}__env`), AND the
            # compose project directory lives in the shared task cache
            # (~/.cache/harbor/tasks/packages/... — `--project-directory
            # <task_cache>/environment`), never under $RUNNER_TEMP/bench.
            # What IS under the bench output: the trial dirs (the -o
            # job dir) bind-mounted into the containers as /logs/* — so
            # the container's .Mounts[].Source is the only harbor-side
            # path under this shard's bench output. Select by the
            # compose project label, then precision-guard on the mount
            # Sources; mount Sources embed the per-registration _temp
            # path, so another workflow's or another registration's
            # live containers are never touched.
            ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project" 2>/dev/null || true)
            torn=0
            for c in $ids; do
              srcs=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null || true)
              for s in $srcs; do
                case "$s" in
                  "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"/*)
                    docker rm -f "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                    torn=$((torn + 1))
                    break ;;
                esac
              done
            done
            if [ "$torn" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "tore down $torn bench container(s) bound to ${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench"
            fi
          fi
          rm -rf "${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench" 2>/dev/null \
            || echo "::warning::${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/bench not fully removable — a container still holds it (gh-1600)"

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # gh-1682: the leaderboard step commits the updated fa-results
    # ledger + regenerated README table back to the repo.

Now some deeper issues to consider:

**Issue A — export exec runs as the agent user with the agent's environment.** `exec_as_agent` runs the command as the agent user. The export needs to read the session JSONL in `/logs/agent/fah-sessions`. Fine.

**Issue B — export exec timeout double-bounded**: `asyncio.wait_for(exec_as_agent(..., timeout_sec=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SEC), timeout=_ATIF_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SEC + 15)`. exec_as_agent with timeout_sec=180 presumably kills the in-container exec after 180s; wait_for cancels at 195s. OK.

**Issue C — CanceledError swallowing**: `except Exception` doesn't catch CanceledError in Python 3.8+ (CancelledError is BaseException). So if the run() task is cancelled while `_export_atif_trajectory` is awaiting, CanceledError propagates — good (finally during cancellation: the export runs to completion then re-raises CanceledError; but wait — the test_external_cancel_still_exports_atif asserts export runs on cancel. In Python, when the outer task is cancelled, `finally:` runs, and awaits inside finally are allowed... but a second cancel would interrupt. The test passes presumably. Note: since Python 3.8, awaiting inside a finally after CanceledError works but if the task was cancelled, the wait_for inside may get cancelled again? The test asserts it works. OK.)

**Issue D — nested cancel risk**: if cancellation arrives during export, `except Exception` won't swallow it. Good.

**Issue E — `_export_atif_trajectory` after crash of `_run_inner`**: if `_run_inner` raised, finally runs export; if export raises (it can't — caught), fine.
